questions.prompt: What is the strongest reason to split an Angular app into micro frontends?

options.text: It always makes the app load faster
Several teams need to build and deploy their parts independently
It removes the need for a design system
Angular apps can't be lazy-loaded otherwise

questions.explanation: Micro frontends are mainly an organizational pattern. They usually cost performance and consistency, so they pay off when teams truly need independent deploys.

questions.prompt: Which split follows the 'slice vertically' rule?

options.text: A header micro frontend, a forms micro frontend, and a services micro frontend
One micro frontend per CSS framework
An exercise-catalog micro frontend and a checkout micro frontend, each with its own UI, state, and API calls

questions.explanation: Vertical slices cover a whole business capability, so each team can ship features alone. Horizontal slices need several teams for every change.

questions.prompt: Match each part of an Angular component to what Angular Elements turns it into.

pairs.right: A maxItems property and a max-items attribute
A 'saved' CustomEvent with the value in event.detail
A custom element registered with customElements.define()

questions.explanation: Inputs become properties (and dash-case attributes), outputs become DOM CustomEvents, and the component is registered as a custom element.

questions.prompt: An Angular host must load an Angular Element built with the CLI's application builder. Which are needed? (Select all that apply)

options.text: Build the element zoneless so the page doesn't get two copies of zone.js
Add CUSTOM_ELEMENTS_SCHEMA to the host component that uses the tag
Declare the element's component in the host's NgModule

questions.explanation: Only one zone.js can run per page, the builder outputs ES modules, and the host compiler must accept the unknown tag. The host never imports the element's component.

questions.prompt: Which function from @angular/elements wraps a component so it can be registered as a custom element?
questions.explanation: createCustomElement(Component, { injector }) returns a class you pass to customElements.define().

questions.prompt: Why should each micro frontend release be deployed to a versioned URL like /mfe/exercise-form/1.4.0/main.js?

options.text: Browsers refuse to load unversioned scripts
So the host can pin, upgrade, and roll back deliberately instead of being broken by another team's deploy or by stale caches

questions.explanation: With outputHashing set to none, versioned paths are what keep caching and independent deploys safe.
